text:
maya: heads-up — i'm hitting a bunch of schema/typing mismatches from function/tool calling outputs. model sometimes returns numbers as strings and streaming partials break json parsing. filed a draft PR with a few helpers: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/987 

alex: repro'd locally. example: 
```ts
const schema = z.object({ count: z.number().int() });
await client.callFunction('count_items', { q }, { expect: schema });
// model returns { "count": "5" } -> zod throws
```

alex: also saw streaming responses that emit `{"count":` in one chunk and `"5"}` later — naive json.parse on partials fails. :grimacing:

jamie: thanks for catching. want to avoid silent data corruption but also reduce friction. proposal: SDK exposes two things — (1) a coercion option that will attempt to coerce types according to the provided schema (opt-in), and (2) a streaming json helper that buffers until a balanced json object is observed, then applies schema validation/coercion.

noah: +1 on opt-in. my vote: default stays strict so we don't silently accept bad formats. add telemetry when coercion runs so we can monitor frequency.

maya: PR tries to add `coerceTypes: boolean` on the call options and a `parseStreamingJson(stream, opts)` util. tests included for number-as-string and null-as-empty-string cases. question for reviewers: should coercion be shallow-only or recursive? thoughts?

alex: recursive makes sense for nested objects but keep it limited (eg. primitives coercion: string->number, string->boolean, number->string). for arrays, coerce elements where schema indicates. also add a fast-fail flag: `coerceStrict: true` that will coerce but still fail if the final type cannot be reconciled.

jamie: for TS devs we can integrate with zod's `coerce` helpers: `z.coerce.number()` etc. For users who pass a runtime schema (zod, yup, json-schema) try to detect and apply library-specific coercion when the flag is set. fallback: a small built-in coercer that understands basic json-schema types.

noah: python note: pydantic v1 has `parse_obj` that will coerce some types; v2 behavior differs. we should doc per-language behavior. maybe add `client.config.coerce_types=True` for parity across SDKs.

maya: another streaming edge: when function/tool calling returns structured output in text streaming mode we sometimes get trailing text after the json object (e.g., logs). propose util tries to find the first balanced top-level object and ignore trailing garbage, with an opt-in `allow_trailing=true`.

alex: agree but default should be false. and warn in logs/metrics when trailing data is dropped. add unit tests that include malformed streams and partial bracket pairs.

jamie: i'll sketch the `parseStreamingJson` signature: 
```ts
parseStreamingJson(stream: AsyncIterable<string>, opts?: { schema?: ZodTypeAny, coerce?: boolean, allowTrailing?: boolean }) => Promise<any>
```
It buffers until top-level braces match, then parse + validate/coerce.

maya: thanks. i'll update PR to: default strict, opt-in coerceTypes, `coerceStrict` fast-fail option, telemetry on coercion and trailing data dropped, and add language notes for python/ts.

ci-bot: build passed for branch feature/sdk-coercion (tests 122/122) :white_check_mark:

alex: nice. i'll review tomorrow morning. pinging @jamie @noah for any last architecture concerns.

jamie: small nit — add an example in the docs showing `coerceTypes` on and off with sample outputs. quick copy suggestion I can add in a follow-up.

noah: thanks maya — this will save a lot of friction when onboarding models that aren't strict about types.

maya: i'll iterate on the PR now and post updates here. planning an async review by 11am PT tomorrow. :pray:
